clue.text: Talk in which girl says she rambles, as 6 complains about cooking ingredient

indicators.note: in which says the talk word is a container with the next piece set inside it

parts.note: a parley is a talk or discussion, especially between opponents

indicators.note: rambles says the letters of the following words wander out of their order

explanation.surface: A conversation in which some girl goes on and on, while a poet moans about a kitchen herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambles' scrambles the three words, and 'in which' sets them inside the word for talk. 6 is 6-down, Ogden Nash, whose famous couplet on the herb misspells the rhyme on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden Nash's famous couplet complaining about the garnish is quoted here, so the definition points to his own line.

clue.text: Part of the body, the sound of Peking?

parts.note: Peking said out loud is P plus King, and the King is Elvis, so the letter P plus Elvis

explanation.surface: A body part, and the noise of a Chinese capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Hear Peking as 'P-king': the King is Elvis Presley, whose hip-swivelling earned him a nickname naming this bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony basin around the hips is a part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Step down first of stairs to break rule

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so the letter goes in

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word stairs

explanation.surface: Stepping down the first stair to defy the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' puts S inside REIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping down from a post means quitting it, giving it up.

clue.text: Love all? Take less time and skill — mixed doubles

indicators.note: mixed says the letters are scrambled together

parts.note: love all is a tennis score of zero each, written as two O's

indicators.note: less says the letter for time is taken away from take

explanation.surface: Tennis talk: love all, then take less time and play skilfully in mixed doubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes T from TAKE to give AKE; 'mixed' rearranges OO, AKE and SKILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is someone who looks just like another person, a lookalike.

clue.text: Poet finds the mark of a leech on food

parts.note: a leech bite leaves a Y-shaped mark
eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: A poet discovers that a leech has left its mark on his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A leech's three jaws leave a Y-shaped wound.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was a celebrated Irish poet, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Enjoying oneself? Good man!

parts.note: bon is French for good
a king is a man, a piece, in chess

explanation.surface: A cheeky exclamation, praising a fellow who is having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enjoying oneself?' is a coy British slang sense for having sex; the question mark flags the euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for having sex, which the clue coyly calls a way of having fun.

clue.text: Poking bottom, I react badly, finding E coli, perhaps?

indicators.note: poking says the rearranged letters push their way inside

parts.note: bum is British slang for bottom

indicators.note: badly says the letters of I react are put into a poor order

explanation.surface: Something prodding my behind makes me react badly: an E coli infection?
explanation.walkthrough: 'E coli, perhaps' is a definition by example; the 'perhaps' admits the germ is only one instance. 'badly' rearranges the letters of I REACT, and 'Poking' sends them into the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: E coli is a single-celled microbe, an example of the germ in question.

clue.text: Partial to pavilion, as Hanoverian architect

indicators.note: Partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has a soft spot for the Brighton Pavilion, as does its Hanoverian architect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial to' looks like 'fond of', but signals a part of the words. John Nash designed the Royal Pavilion in Brighton, a seaside town, for the Hanoverian Prince Regent.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash, the Regency architect of Brighton's Royal Pavilion, is an example of an architect.

clue.text: King held up by goddess for nationals

indicators.note: held says the goddess's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Isis is an Egyptian goddess

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A king is held up by a goddess on behalf of a nation's people.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the king's name, and 'held' has the goddess wrap it. Lear is the elderly monarch of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of Israel are nationals of that country.

clue.text: See 20
Lady requiring oxygen for something catching?

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A woman who needs oxygen, perhaps because she has something infectious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something catching' looks like a disease; the question mark warns it is a rope used to catch cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed rope is thrown to catch animals, so it is literally a thing for catching.

clue.text: Family trips not starting, I abandon path

indicators.note: not starting says the opening letter of the word for trips is dropped

parts.note: trips, as in tripping the light fantastic, are dances

indicators.note: abandon tells us the letter I is removed from the word for path

parts.note: a trail is a path

explanation.surface: Someone renounces the family journeys and leaves a well-trodden route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' turns DANCES into ANCES; 'abandon' takes I out of TRAIL, leaving TRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something inherited down a line of forebears, so belonging to a family.

clue.text: See 1
Grouse to swallow?

definitions.meaning: to grouse is to grumble, and a grumble is slang for a complaint
meat from cattle is something one eats and swallows

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a complaint or grievance, and also the meat of cattle, eaten as food.

clue.text: Pulse -— bendy sort — pulse, ultimately, one gobbled by family

indicators.note: gobbled by says the pieces are swallowed inside the word for family

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: sort says the letters of bendy are sorted into a new order
ultimately points to the last letter of the second pulse

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A bendy type of pulse, and ultimately one gets eaten up by the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Pulse' is the definition; the second only lends its last letter. 'sort' rearranges BENDY, and 'gobbled by' puts the pieces inside the family word.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume seed, a kidney-shaped one, is an example of a pulse.

clue.text: Impairments stabilised, one doubly mobile

indicators.note: mobile says the letters are free to move into a new arrangement
doubly says the letter for one is used twice

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Disabled conditions have been steadied, though one person is still very much on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives II, which joins STABILISED before 'mobile' rearranges all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions limiting physical or mental function are impairments, a near synonym.

clue.text: Sea with exclamation of discovery about bats being upside-down — or, perhaps, 6 on 23?

indicators.note: upside-down in a down clue says the whole thing is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: about says the exclamation goes round the word for bats

parts.note: aha is what one cries on discovering something
bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A sea, a cry of discovery, and some bats hanging upside-down: perhaps a poem about insects?
explanation.walkthrough: MED + AH(MAD)A gives MEDAHMADA; 'being upside-down' reverses it all. 6 is NASH and 23 is FLEAS: the famous two-line poem on that subject, often credited to Nash.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny verse on fleas, often credited to Ogden Nash, consists entirely of these words.

clue.text: 20 8 by 6, perhaps, or from the poet Whitehead?

indicators.note: from says the letters come out of the poet and the head of White, rearranged

parts.note: the head of White is its first letter, W

explanation.surface: A poem by a famous humorist, or perhaps one taken from a poet called Whitehead?
explanation.walkthrough: THE POET plus W is rearranged by 'from'. 20 8 is 20-down with 8-down, a tiny poem whose whole text is these three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The miniature goldfish poem, credited perhaps to Nash, consists of just these words.

clue.text: Happy house passed around by rising river — that's extreme happiness!

indicators.note: passed around by says the other pieces are enclosed by the river
rising in a down clue says the river's name is read upwards

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
up can mean happy, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: A contented household is surrounded by a swelling river, and they are thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England. 'rising' turns its name upwards, and 'passed around by' has it enclose the two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense elation or bliss is extreme happiness.

clue.text: Get-together — in what way a hive of activity, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say tells us the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.words: in what way a hive of activity
parts.note: in what way is how, and a hive of activity is swarming, giving the phrase how swarming

explanation.surface: A party question: how is the place buzzing like a beehive?
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, HOW SWARMING runs together into the name of a party to celebrate a new home.
explanation.definitionFit: A party thrown to celebrate moving into a new home is a type of social get-together.

clue.text: Bully's heartless right-wing bombast

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letters are taken out

parts.note: Tory means right-wing, a member of the UK Conservative Party
a rant is bombastic speech

explanation.surface: A bully's cruel conservative rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes OR from TORY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel, oppressive ruler or person who domineers over others is a bully.

clue.text: Good deal of this ornate creation of 6, perhaps

indicators.note: ornate suggests the letters are elaborately rearranged

explanation.surface: Much of this decorative work was made by an architect, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is NASH; the 'creation' looks like a Nash building, but the definition points to the poet. 'ornate' rearranges GOOD DEAL OF THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny verse addressed to a pet fish, here credited perhaps to Ogden Nash, is his creation.

clue.text: Bouncer releasing king from impossible choke

indicators.note: impossible signals the remaining letters should be rearranged
releasing a thing from somewhere lets it out, so that letter is removed
releasing a thing from somewhere lets it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the forward run across impossible choke is a coincidence: the setter's parse removes the king and rearranges
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman lets a king out of a stranglehold that cannot be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' K 'from' CHOKE leaves CHOE, which 'impossible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound bounces back off a surface, so it is a thing that bounces.

clue.text: Suspicious-looking, fishy, yet astonishing journalist

indicators.note: astonishing suggests the words are thrown into disarray and rearranged

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Something is dubious, and yet a reporter is amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astonishing' rearranges the letters of FISHY and YET; the journalist abbreviation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose gaze darts about appears evasive and untrustworthy, which is suspicious-looking.

clue.text: Unwelcome visitors, first of aliens being upset about it

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the letter
upset in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: a self is one's being

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of aliens

explanation.surface: Unwanted guests: the first of the aliens being disturbed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SELF into FLES, which goes 'about' the A of aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodsucking insects that infest pets and homes are unwelcome visitors.

clue.text: Three's crowd trouble, if head to toe

indicators.note: if head to toe says one letter moves between the top and the bottom of the word

parts.note: a riot is trouble from a crowd

explanation.surface: Three people make a crowd, the old saying goes, and trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two's company, three's a crowd' is the proverb the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three, especially musicians, is three people.

clue.text: Bird perhaps, given malicious gossip, hit back

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: eg, for example, means perhaps
dirt is scandalous or malicious gossip
to rap is to hit

explanation.surface: A bird, given some nasty rumours, strikes back at them.
explanation.walkthrough: EG, DIRT and RAP give EGDIRTRAP; 'back' reverses the whole string. 'Bird perhaps' looks like one unit, but 'perhaps' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump game bird of fields and hedgerows, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Old key for lift

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: An outdated key once used for a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise up or elevate, in praise or rank, is to lift.

clue.text: Male fed a bit of corn oil primarily, where cakes available?

indicators.note: fed says the male is given the other pieces inside him

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
an ear is part of a cereal plant like corn

indicators.note: primarily says just the first letter of oil is taken

explanation.surface: A man feeds on a bit of corn, mostly oil; is this where cakes are to be found?
explanation.walkthrough: 'where cakes available?' is a definition by description. 'fed' has the male cat take in the corn piece and the first letter of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A small café serving tea and cakes is where cakes are on offer.

clue.text: Star turn in a star

indicators.note: turn tells us the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity performs an act inside a famous celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges STAR IN A; the second 'star' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank the crooner was a famous singing and film celebrity.
